name: ROSETTA
aliases: Refractory Overactive Bladder: Sacral NEuromodulation vs BoTulinum Toxin Assessment
question: Does 200 U intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA reduce urgency urinary incontinence more than staged sacral neuromodulation in women with refractory symptoms?

design.population: 386 randomized women at nine US centers with at least six urgency-incontinence episodes on a three-day diary despite supervised behavioral or physical therapy and at least two anticholinergics or inability to use them.

verdictNote: The six-month episode difference was 0.63 per day; infection and catheterization were more frequent with toxin.
takeaway: In women with refractory urgency urinary incontinence, one 200 U onabotulinumtoxinA injection reduced daily episodes slightly more over six months than staged InterStim sacral neuromodulation (3.9 versus 3.3 fewer; mean difference 0.63), with more urinary tract infections and intermittent catheterization.

delivery.label: Operator experience and standardized techniques
delivery.value: Implanters had performed at least 10 InterStim procedures and injectors at least 10 toxin procedures; both reviewed standardized technique videos.

delivery.label: SNM test and implantation
delivery.value: First-stage lead placement under local and monitored anesthesia care, intraoperative sensory and motor testing, then a 7–14-day test; at least 50% diary reduction qualified for permanent generator implantation.

delivery.label: Injection and postvoid residual protocol
delivery.value: Clinic cystoscopic intradetrusor injection of 200 U; intermittent catheterization for residual greater than 300 mL, or greater than 200 mL with incomplete-voiding symptoms.

delivery.label: Treatment received and initial response
delivery.value: 189/192 randomized to toxin received the full injection and 159/192 (83%) responded; 169/189 eligible assigned to SNM had stage-one placement, 142/169 (84%) responded, and 139 received the permanent generator.
delivery.locator: JAMA PDF p 5, Figure 1 and Results; journal p 1370

delivery.label: Repeat toxin injection
delivery.value: 115/159 (72%) initial toxin responders requested a second injection; median first-to-second interval 350 days. Of those 115, 101 received 200 U and 14 were dose-reduced to 100 U after prolonged catheterization.

delivery.label: SNM reprogramming
delivery.value: 81/139 (58%) implanted initial responders needed reprogramming during 24 months.

reports.citation: Getaneh FW, Kolm P, Awulachew H, et al. "Comparing Impact of Overactive Bladder Therapies on Nocturia." *Urogynecology (Phila).* 2024;30(3):264-271. doi:10.1097/SPV.0000000000001465
reports.followUp: Six months among participants with at least two nocturnal voids on a three-day diary
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Materials and Methods, pp 265–266

results.measure: Mean voids per night at baseline and six months, with adjusted change from the repeated-measures model; P value compares change across all four ABC and ROSETTA cohorts

values.exp: 200 U toxin: 2.8 ± 1.0 to 1.9 ± 1.2 voids/night; adjusted change −1.1 ± 0.2 (32% decrease; cohort n=63, Table 2 n=62)
values.ctl: sacral neuromodulation: 3.0 ± 1.1 to 2.0 ± 1.4 voids/night; adjusted change −0.9 ± 0.2 (33% decrease; n=54)

results.note: Primary outcome of this secondary analysis. The four-cohort comparison is not a ROSETTA pairwise test. Across 197 included women, mean voids/night fell 41%, from 2.7 ± 0.4 to 1.6 ± 0.5 (P<0.001); adjusted changes were −1.3 ± 0.3 with anticholinergics and −1.2 ± 0.3 with 100 U toxin. No confidence interval for the between-cohort comparison was reported.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 266; Table 2, p 268

results.measure: At most one mean nocturnal void on a follow-up three-day diary; P value compares all four cohorts
results.note: Exploratory resolution analysis; 72/197 (37%) overall, including 14/43 (33%) with anticholinergics and 19/37 (51%) with 100 U toxin. The P value is for all four cohorts, not a ROSETTA pairwise test.
results.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 266; Results, p 267
